inline.s: [This is called the first expedient of the three contemplations.]
This is the first expedient of the three contemplations. (Answering the question, “Of the three pure contemplations, which is taken as the first?”)
[First expedient]The expedient for the initial attainment of the Way.

[If sentient beings universally cultivate the three contemplations and diligently practice vigor, this is called the Tathagata appearing in the world. If again sentient beings of dull faculties in the last age, with minds wishing to seek the Way, are unable to attain success, because of past karmic obstacles they should diligently repent. Constantly arousing hope, they should first cut off hatred and love, envy, sycophancy and crookedness, and the mind that seeks to surpass [others]. Of the three pure contemplations, they should practice one matter as taught. If this contemplation is not attained, then cultivate that contemplation; not letting go of the mind, they seek its realization step by step.]

If sentient beings universally cultivate the three contemplations and diligently practice vigor, this is called the Tathagata appearing in the world. If sentient beings of dull faculties in the last age, with minds wishing to seek the Way, are unable to attain success, this is due to karmic obstacles from the past, and so they should diligently add repentance. Constantly arousing hope and wishing to cut off karmic obstacles, they should first cut off hatred and love, envy, sycophancy and crookedness, as well as the arrogant mind that seeks to surpass all others. Of the three pure contemplations, they should study one gate as it suits them. If they cannot get a start in this contemplation, then take up another contemplation; not letting go of the mind, they seek its realization step by step.

[Perfect Enlightenment, you should know: all sentient beings, if they wish to seek the unsurpassed Way, should first enter the three periods. Repenting the karma without beginning, passing through twenty-one days, then engage in right reflection. The realms not heard by them can never be taken up.]

Perfect Enlightenment, you should know: all sentient beings, if they wish to seek the unsurpassed Way, should first enter the three periods (one hundred twenty days, or one hundred days, or eighty days). Repenting the karma without beginning, passing through twenty-one days, then engage in right reflection. Unless the realms are those heard above (the World-Honored One's instructions in the preceding ten chapters), none of them are to be taken up.

[Samatha is the utmost stillness, samapatti is right recollection and holding, dhyana is the gate of counting; these are called the three pure contemplations. If one can diligently cultivate them, this is called the Buddha appearing in the world. For those of dull faculties who have not yet succeeded, always diligently repent the whole karma without beginning. If all the obstacles are eliminated, the Buddha-realm appears before one.]

Samatha is the utmost stillness, samapatti is right recollection and holding, dhyana is the gate of counting; these are called the three pure contemplations. If one can diligently cultivate these three pure contemplations, this is called the Buddha appearing in the world. For those of dull faculties who have not yet succeeded, always diligently repent in mind all the karmic offenses without beginning. If all the obstacles are eliminated, the Buddha-realm appears before one.

blocks.text: 1. The Five Questions of the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou

inline.s: [Thereupon, in the midst of the assembly, the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou rose from his seat, touched his head to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, knelt long with hands folded, and said to the Buddha: Greatly compassionate World-Honored One, you have broadly opened and awakened such an inconceivable matter for us and for sentient beings of the last age. World-Honored One, what is the name of this Mahayana teaching, and how should it be upheld? What merit do sentient beings gain by cultivating it? How should we protect the one who upholds this sutra? To what stage does circulating this teaching reach? Having spoken these words, he prostrated his whole body on the ground. He made this request three times, ending and beginning again.]

Thereupon, in the midst of the assembly, the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou rose from his seat, touched his head to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, knelt long with hands folded, and respectfully said to the Buddha: Greatly compassionate World-Honored One, you have broadly opened and caused us to enter into such an inconceivable matter for us and for sentient beings of the last age. World-Honored One, what is the name of this Mahayana sutra, and how should it be upheld? What merit do sentient beings gain by cultivating this sutra? How should we protect the one who upholds this sutra? Circulating this teaching and cultivating it thus, will it reach what stage (that is, what fruit-position will it reach)? Having spoken these words, the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou prostrated his whole body on the ground. He made this request three times, ending and beginning again.

[At that time, the World-Honored One said to the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou: Good! Good! Good man. You are able, for the sake of the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask the Tathagata about the merit and the name of this sutra-teaching. Listen well now, and I shall speak it for you. At that time, the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou, delighting in receiving the instruction, and the great assembly, listened in silence.]

At that time, the World-Honored One said to the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou: Excellent! Excellent! Good man. You are able, for the sake of the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age, to ask the Tathagata about the merit and the name of this sutra-teaching. Now gather your minds and listen carefully; I shall proclaim it for you. At that time, the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou, delighting in receiving the instruction, and the great assembly, listened in silence.

[Good man! This sutra was spoken by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, is guarded by the Tathagatas of the three times, is relied upon by the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, and is the pure eye of the twelve categories of scriptures. The name of this sutra is the Great, Vast, Perfect Enlightenment Dharani; it is also called the Ultimate Meaning of the Sutras; it is also called the King of Secret Samadhi; it is also called the Determined Realm of the Tathagata; it is also called the Distinctions of the Self-Nature of the Tathagata-Store. You should uphold it.]

Good man! This sutra was spoken by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, is guarded by the Tathagatas of the three times, is relied upon by the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, and is the pure eye of the twelve categories of scriptures. The name of this sutra is the Great, Vast, Perfect Enlightenment Dharani; it is also called the Ultimate Meaning of the Sutras; it is also called the King of Secret Samadhi; it is also called the Determined Realm of the Tathagata; it is also called the Distinctions of the Self-Nature of the Tathagata-Store. You should uphold it as such.

[Good man! This sutra alone reveals the Tathagata's realm; only the Buddha-Tathagata can fully proclaim it. If the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age cultivate according to this, advancing gradually, they will reach the Buddha-ground.]

Good man! This sutra alone reveals the Tathagata's realm; only the Buddhas and Tathagatas can proclaim it penetratingly. If the bodhisattvas and the sentient beings of the last age cultivate according to this, advancing gradually, they can reach the Buddha-ground. (Answering the Bodhisattva Xianshanshou's earlier question, “To what stage does it reach?”)

blocks.text: 4. Both Sudden and Gradual Are Included

inline.s: [Good man! This sutra is called the Sudden Teaching of the Great Vehicle; sentient beings of sudden faculties awaken from it. It also includes all the groups of beings who cultivate gradually. It is like the great ocean, which does not refuse small streams. Even to mosquitos and asuras, those who drink its water all become filled.]

Good man! This sutra is called the Sudden Teaching of the Great Vehicle; sentient beings of sudden faculties awaken according to it. This sutra also includes the various types of beings who cultivate gradually. It is like the great ocean, which does not abandon the small rivers. Even to mosquitoes (a metaphor for the very small) and asuras (a metaphor for the very great), those who drink its water all become filled in their bellies.
[All the groups of beings]Sentient beings of various faculties.
[Good man! Suppose someone used only the seven treasures to fill the entire trichiliocosm as a gift; it would not equal someone hearing the name of this sutra and the meaning of a single phrase.]

Good man! Suppose someone used only the seven treasures to fill the entire trichiliocosm and used them as gifts; it would not equal someone hearing the name of this sutra and the principle of a single phrase of its text.
This paragraph and the following answer the question, “What merit do sentient beings gain by cultivating it?”

[Good man! Suppose someone taught hundreds of thousands of sentient beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to attain the fruit of arhatship; it would not equal someone proclaiming this sutra and explaining half a verse.]

Good man! Suppose someone taught hundreds of thousands of sentient beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to attain the fruit of arhatship; it would not equal someone proclaiming this sutra and clarifying half a verse.

[Good man! If again someone hears the name of this sutra and has faith without confusion, you should know that this person has planted blessings and wisdom not merely before one Buddha or two Buddhas, but thus even down to having planted wholesome roots before all the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and so is able to hear this sutra-teaching.]

Good man! If again someone hears the name of this sutra and has faith without confusion, you should know that this person has planted blessings and wisdom not merely before one Buddha or two Buddhas, nor merely before three Buddhas or four Buddhas, but thus even down to having planted wholesome roots before Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, indeed before all the Buddhas, and so is able to hear this sutra-teaching and have faith without confusion.
[You good men should protect these practitioners of the last age, and not let evil demons and the various heretics disturb their body and mind and cause them to retreat.]

You good men should protect these practitioners of the last age (those who have heard the name of this sutra and have faith without confusion), and by no means let evil demons and the various heretics disturb their body and mind and cause them to retreat.

[At that time, in the assembly there were the Fire-Headed Vajra, the Crushing Vajra, the Nilamba Vajra, and other eighty thousand vajras with their retinues, who rose from their seats, touched their heads to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, if in the last age there are sentient beings able to uphold this Determined Great Vehicle, we shall guard them as we guard our own eyes. Even at the places of the bodhimanda where they cultivate, we vajras will ourselves lead our followers to guard them morning and evening, causing them not to retreat. Their homes will be forever free of disasters and hindrances; epidemics will be eradicated; treasure and wealth will be abundant, never lacking.]

At that time, in the assembly there were the Fire-Headed Vajra, the Crushing Vajra, the Nilamba Vajra, and other eighty thousand vajras with their retinues, who rose from their seats, touched their heads to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and respectfully said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, if in the last age there are sentient beings able to uphold this sutra of the Determined Great Vehicle, we shall guard them strictly, as we protect the pupils of our own eyes. Even at the places of the bodhimanda where they cultivate, we vajras will ourselves lead our followers to guard them day and night, causing them not to retreat. Their homes will be forever free of disasters and hindrances; epidemics will be eradicated; treasure and wealth will be abundant, always rich.

[At that time, the Great Brahma king, the twenty-eight heaven-kings, and the king of Mount Sumeru, the state-protecting heaven-kings, and others rose from their seats, touched their heads to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, we too shall guard these upholders of the sutra, always causing them to be at peace and their minds not to retreat.]

At that time, the Great Brahma king, the twenty-eight heaven-kings, and the king of Mount Sumeru, the state-protecting heaven-kings, and others rose from their seats, touched their heads to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and respectfully said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, we too shall guard these upholders of the sutra (the ones who uphold this sutra), always causing them to be at peace and their minds not to retreat.

[At that time, there was a powerful ghost king named Jipantu, with a hundred thousand ghost kings, who rose from their seats, touched their heads to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, we too shall guard these upholders of the sutra, attending them morning and evening, causing them not to retreat. If, within one yojana of the place where they dwell, any ghost or spirit invades their realm, we shall grind it to dust as fine as motes.]

At that time, there was a powerful ghost king named Jipantu, with a hundred thousand ghost kings, who rose from their seats, touched their heads to the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and respectfully said to the Buddha: World-Honored One, we too shall guard these upholders of the sutra, attending them morning and evening, causing them not to retreat. If, within one yojana of the place where they dwell, any ghost or spirit invades their realm, we shall grind them to dust as fine as motes.
[Yojana]A unit of distance in India. There are three sizes: a great yojana is about eighty li; a middle yojana about sixty li; a small yojana about forty li.

[When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, all the bodhisattvas, the devas, dragons, ghosts, and spirits, the eight classes and their retinues, and the various heaven-kings, Brahma kings, and the whole assembly, having heard what the Buddha said, all rejoiced greatly, believed, received, and practiced it.]

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, all the bodhisattvas, the devas, dragons, ghosts, and spirits, the eight classes and their retinues, and the various heaven-kings, Brahma kings, and the whole assembly, having heard what the Buddha said, all rejoiced greatly, believed, received, and practiced it.

[Devas and dragons]The deva assembly and the dragon assembly are two of the eight classes. [Eight classes]The deva assembly, the dragon assembly, the yakshas (rendered “brave ghosts” in Chinese), the gandharvas (rendered “fragrant spirits” in Chinese), the asuras (rendered “non-gods” in Chinese), the garudas (rendered “golden-winged birds” in Chinese), the kimnaras (rendered “non-humans” in Chinese), and the mahoragas (rendered “great python spirits” or “great-bellied earth-dragons” in Chinese). Because the eyes of human beings cannot see them, they are also called “the eight classes of the unseen assembly.” And because among the eight classes the devas and dragons are the most excellent, they are also called “the eight classes of devas and dragons,” or “the eight classes of dragon-spirits.”
